record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the complete post, but the graphs it describes are not included, so their plotted values are unavailable.
record.tranche_reason: Tests grokking and a training-time progress measure on modular arithmetic, but uses a multi-problem setup and reports loss and LLC curves rather than the original accuracy-based measurements.
record.gate_note: The post reports qualitative results from test-loss and LLC curves. It does not report training or test accuracy values, and the training set size is fixed at 16900 rather than varied. It also describes trying different optimizers and other techniques in response to loss spikes, but reports no controlled result showing that optimizer or numerical choices produce or eliminate grokking.
record.test_reason: A new setting: one transformer learns modular addition and multiplication together. The post reports its own memorize-then-generalize test-loss curves, separately per operation and across task ratios. The evidence is qualitative and loss-based, with no accuracy values and a fixed training-set size.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author also says the two operations showed distinct grokking behaviours that depended on the training ratio. The initial hypothesis, that these would produce separate LLC stages, was not borne out: there was a single LLC decline.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a toy transformer on modular arithmetic in a grokking setup, but trains on addition and multiplication together, varies their ratio, keeps the training set at 16900 problems, and measures LLC and test loss. The post describes its setup as similar to the cited grokking work but does not give enough detail to establish an exact match.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported timing of LLC decline varies with the addition-to-multiplication ratio. The author also reports loss spikes and says LLC estimation is sensitive to estimation hyperparameters, without reporting quantified comparisons for those choices.

fits_no_version.finding: LLC rises during overfitting, then shows a single decline during generalization. The decline starts earlier for more uneven task ratios, and no separate developmental stages appear for the two operations.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Grokking coincides with a single phase transition in LLC (model complexity), even when two tasks grok at different times.

record.problems: Loss spikes and noisy curves complicate interpretation. Numerical curve values, accuracy values, and uncertainty estimates are absent from the supplied text. The training set size is not varied.
record.rows_left_out: No reported result rows were omitted. Ratio-specific plotted values are unavailable in the supplied text, so R3 records the post's aggregate qualitative comparison rather than separate numerical rows.

Identification of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, and whether a continuous measure anticipates the jump.
Loss spikes persisted across optimizers and schedulers, but there is no controlled test of whether optimizer or numerical choices produce the delay.

record.verdict_notes: This is a short LessWrong capstone post. All figures are absent from the text, so no numerical values can be read. The reader's V2 'supports' label is dropped: LLC tracks generalization but is not shown to anticipate it, and no circuit is examined. The slingshot mechanism is mentioned only as speculation about the loss spikes.

Does not identify a generalizing circuit, track memorizing components being removed, or establish that LLC decline precedes an accuracy jump.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm intervention.
No LLM or realistic large-model training.
No test of weight decay or another low-norm bias, critical dataset size, or ungrokking.

rows.subject: single layer transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Evaluated test loss separately on modular addition and multiplication test sets during training.
rows.measure: Test loss curves; the post says grokking behavior differed by problem type and training-data ratio.
rows.value: The post reports separate grokking behavior for the two problem types, varying with their proportions in the training data.
rows.note: The post describes initial memorization followed by gradual generalization, but supplies no accuracy values or plotted loss values in the provided text. The result is qualitative and does not test the effect of shrinking the training set.
rows.check: The author states plainly that training followed a grokking pattern: memorization, then generalization. So the delayed generalization itself is observed, not partial. The size-dependence part of V1 is untested rather than partially shown. The measure is test loss, not accuracy, and no values are given because the figures are missing.

rows.subject: single layer transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Measured local learning coefficient (LLC) during training.
rows.value: The LLC rose rapidly as the model overfit the training data, then declined as it generalized on both addition and multiplication.
rows.note: This is a qualitative progress measure; the supplied text gives no numerical LLC values and does not show that the decline precedes an accuracy jump.
rows.check: LLC rises during overfitting and falls during generalization. That fall happens alongside generalization. The post gives no timing of LLC against the test-loss drop, no circuit identification and no removal of memorizing components, so it cannot show the progress measure anticipating the jump.

rows.subject: single layer transformer model
rows.operation_detail: Compared LLC curves across training-data ratios.
rows.value: The post reports that more uneven ratios began declining earlier; this mirrored faster grokking by the dominant problem type. The overall LLC curve shape was described as similar across ratios.
rows.note: The comparison is reported qualitatively across ratios; exact ratio-specific LLC values and timings are not present in the supplied text.
rows.check: The earlier LLC decline for uneven ratios is described as mirroring faster grokking, which is co-occurrence, not anticipation. No values are given. This bears mainly on the author's own developmental-stage hypothesis.

relationships.condition: 1-layer transformer, joint modular addition/multiplication mod 113, 16900 training problems, 30–70% addition
relationships.reason: The author reports memorization followed by later generalization in test loss for each operation, with timing varying by task ratio (R1). The evidence is qualitative and loss-based only.
relationships.display_finding: Both operations showed memorization followed by later test-loss improvement, with generalization timing varying with the training task ratio.
